narrativeReportMd:
# canonical R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking change was found for the `canonical` primitive. The datatype keeps the same identity, cardinalities, underlying FHIRPath string representation, and `\\S*` lexical regex; the only local finding is a low-risk snapshot/codegen metadata correction on `canonical.value`.

## Scope
The analysis covered the assigned R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition/canonical` files, package indexes, package metadata, the batch manifest, and the direct `uri` base to distinguish local from inherited changes. Inherited Element/Extension constraints and the R6 primitive infrastructure shift are explicitly out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration is mostly a tooling concern. Existing instance values that are valid `canonical` strings in R4 remain representable in R6, and R6 canonical primitive values remain representable in R4. Implementers who generate code or runtime metadata directly from `snapshot.element[].type.extension[structuredefinition-fhir-type]` should notice that the R6 snapshot now labels `canonical.value` as `canonical`, whereas the R4 snapshot labels it as `string` even though the R4 differential already said `canonical`.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The single finding is Low impact and affects snapshot-driven code generation or reflection, not wire-format validation.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires human review based on the local computable definitions. Official narrative or ballot notes would mainly improve confidence about the intent behind the metadata additions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 metadata appears to make the snapshot more internally consistent and to expose canonical-specific characteristics (`has-target`, `has-length`). Those additions are backward-compatible for instances; compatibility work belongs in tooling that supports both R4 and R6 metadata shapes.

## Follow-up analysis
Reports for `uri`, `PrimitiveType`, `Element`, and `Extension` should own inherited primitive infrastructure and invariant changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `canonical` has no local hard instance-breaking change from R4 to R6. The top concerns are snapshot-driven code generation seeing `canonical.value` as `canonical` instead of generic `string`, metadata-aware tooling reacting to new R6 type characteristics, and avoiding accidental attribution of inherited `uri`/primitive infrastructure changes to `canonical`. The main uncertainty is the absence of official diff and rendered narrative context for the new metadata.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Instance migration should be straightforward: cardinality, primitive representation, and the `\\S*` lexical regex are unchanged. Tooling migration should focus on version-aware metadata handling: do not infer that R4 canonical values were merely strings because one R4 snapshot extension says `string`, and do not treat the new R6 type-characteristic metadata as a new instance requirement.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local computable comparison because both R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present and the same direct artifact identity is indexed in both packages. Confidence is lower for intent and broader conformance implications because no official change note, rendered narrative page, or local definition for the type-characteristics extension codes was available.

findings.title: canonical.value snapshot FHIR type metadata changed from string to canonical

oldState.summary: The R4 snapshot labels the primitive value's structuredefinition-fhir-type extension as string, while the R4 differential labels it as canonical.
oldState.narrativeMd: In the R4 snapshot, `canonical.value` remains a FHIRPath `System.String` with regex `\\S*`, but its `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension has `valueUrl: string`. The R4 differential for the same element already has `valueUrl: canonical`, so the old artifact is internally inconsistent rather than clearly specifying a different wire format.

newState.summary: The R6 snapshot and differential both label the primitive value's structuredefinition-fhir-type extension as canonical.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `canonical.value` keeps the same FHIRPath `System.String` type and regex `\\S*`, and the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension now consistently identifies the primitive as `canonical` in both snapshot and differential.

facts.note: The underlying ElementDefinition.type.code remains http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String and the lexical regex remains \\S*.
The local differential did not change; R6 makes the generated snapshot agree with the differential.

facts.oldValue: FHIR primitive string value with optional primitive extension object
facts.newValue: FHIR primitive string value with optional primitive extension object
facts.note: No JSON/XML wire-format element was added, removed, or renamed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same id and path, `canonical.value`, with the same cardinality, representation, FHIRPath type code, and regex. The only local delta is the value of a metadata extension in the generated snapshot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an instance-validation break: a canonical primitive value is still serialized as a string-like primitive and the `\\S*` regex is unchanged. The risk is limited to tools that generate primitive wrapper classes, metadata enums, validators, schemas, or reflection APIs from the snapshot extension rather than from the StructureDefinition identity or differential. Such tools may see R4 as generic `string` and R6 as `canonical`, changing generated type names or dispatch paths.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: No clinical or business content is lost by the metadata correction itself. Failures would be build-time or runtime tooling mismatches rather than changed patient data semantics.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the generated snapshot consistently identify the primitive value as canonical rather than generic string.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because the change does not invalidate R4 canonical instances; tooling normalization is a compatibility mitigation, not a base-design alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: make the generated snapshot identify `canonical.value` consistently with the `canonical` datatype identity and with both versions' differentials. The level of breakage is also reasonable because cardinality, FHIRPath value type, lexical regex, and wire format remain unchanged; the risk is limited to metadata-driven code generation or reflection that treated the R4 snapshot quirk as authoritative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. R4 canonical primitive values serialized as strings remain valid and representable in R6. The main compatibility action is for multi-version tools to normalize the R4 snapshot quirk or key primitive identity from the StructureDefinition URL/type; that is migration/tooling mitigation, not an alternative R6 base design. The only spec-design alternative would be to leave the R6 snapshot extension as `string`, which would preserve compatibility for a narrow class of snapshot-only generators while continuing inaccurate metadata for canonical-aware tooling.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the old string snapshot metadata would reduce churn for snapshot-only generators but preserve an internal inconsistency with canonical's datatype identity and differential.

evidence.detail: R4 snapshot metadata labels the primitive value's FHIR type as string.
R6 snapshot metadata labels the primitive value's FHIR type as canonical.
The R4 differential already identifies the primitive value as canonical.
The R6 lexical regex is unchanged from R4.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is provided because the finding is metadata-only. The same JSON primitive value, for example an element value of `http://example.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/foo`, remains string-serialized in both versions.

findings.narrativeMd: `canonical.value` did not gain a new element, cardinality, regex, binding, or wire-format representation. The material local delta is that R6's generated snapshot now says the primitive value has FHIR type `canonical`, while R4's generated snapshot said `string` despite the R4 differential saying `canonical`. Implementers most likely to notice are those that generate code or runtime reflection tables from snapshot metadata and compare primitive types by this extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid canonical value does not become invalid in R6 because of this change, and an R6 canonical value remains representable as an R4 canonical string. The compatibility risk is in tooling behavior: generated classes, schema adapters, or FHIRPath/runtime type switches may route through a canonical-specific type in R6 where an R4 snapshot-driven generator used a generic string path.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Multi-version tooling should key the primitive identity from the StructureDefinition URL/type (`canonical`) and treat `canonical.value` as a string-valued primitive with canonical semantics. If code generators previously consumed only the R4 snapshot extension, add a compatibility normalization so R4 `canonical.value` is not downgraded to an ordinary string when comparing or converting between versions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change appears to correct old snapshot metadata rather than introduce a new datatype shape. Preserving the old `string` value in R6 would be backward-compatible for snapshot consumers but less accurate for canonical-aware tooling. A compatibility layer in generators is the least disruptive approach because it handles both the old snapshot quirk and the more precise R6 metadata.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Both packages contain `StructureDefinition-canonical.json` with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind `primitive-type`, type `canonical`, derivation `specialization`, and direct base `uri`.
The snapshot element ids remain `canonical`, `canonical.id`, `canonical.extension`, and `canonical.value`; the differential element ids remain `canonical` and `canonical.value`.
Local cardinalities are unchanged: root `canonical` is `0..*`, `canonical.value` is `0..1`, and inherited `id` and `extension` cardinalities are unchanged in the snapshots.

The underlying `ElementDefinition.type.code` for `canonical.value` remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`. The only type-related delta is the snapshot metadata extension reported as a codegen finding.

`canonical.value` has no `targetProfile`, aggregation, or versioning list in either StructureDefinition. R6 adds a root type-characteristic metadata code `has-target`, noted separately as non-breaking metadata.
No terminology binding is present on the local canonical elements in either version.
No local canonical-specific invariant was added, removed, or changed. Differences in inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` wording and `xpath` metadata are out of scope.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value appears on the local canonical elements in either version.
The `canonical.value` regex extension remains `\\S*` in both R4 and R6.
`isModifier` remains `false` on all canonical snapshot elements.
`isSummary` remains `false` on all canonical snapshot elements.
No slicing appears on the local canonical elements in either version.

The root short, definition, and comment remain materially the same. The artifact description changes from `Base StructureDefinition for canonical type...` to `canonical type...`, which appears editorial rather than a conformance change.

The primitive value remains represented as an XML attribute and string-valued primitive. Snapshot metadata changed from `string` to `canonical`, which is reported as a low-risk codegen/reflection finding.
No new R6 instance content shape was introduced for the canonical primitive itself. R6 canonical primitive values remain representable as R4 canonical primitive strings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds computable type-characteristic metadata for canonical
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` extension values `has-target` and `has-length` on the `canonical` StructureDefinition. These are artifact metadata, not instance elements, and they do not change the primitive's cardinality, regex, or wire format.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-aware tooling may use `has-target` to treat canonical values more like resolvable canonical references and `has-length` to permit length-related constraints. Multi-version tooling should not interpret the absence of these extension values in R4 as proof that canonical values lack target or length semantics.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds or updates administrative metadata without changing datatype identity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes administrative fields such as publisher, date, `experimental: false`, jurisdiction, generated narrative placeholder, and work-group metadata. The canonical URL, id, type, kind, status, normative status, and direct base remain stable.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that diff raw StructureDefinitions should classify these as package/ballot metadata churn rather than datatype instance-breaking changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `canonical` specializes `uri`; any inherited lexical or base-definition changes to `uri` should be assessed in the `uri` report rather than duplicated here.

R6 primitive datatypes inherit through `PrimitiveType` infrastructure. Class-hierarchy, inherited invariant, and extension behavior changes should be handled by the PrimitiveType/Element/Extension analyses.
